sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Cline is an open-source AI coding agent that works in VS Code, JetBrains IDEs, your terminal and a desktop app. It edits files across your project, runs commands, browses the web and uses tools, asking for your approval along the way, with whichever AI model you choose.
sixtySeconds.problem: Coding assistants that only autocomplete can't carry out multi-step changes, and many agents lock you to one model provider. Cline plans and executes real changes across a codebase and works with Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, local models and more.
whoFor: Developers who want an AI agent inside VS Code or JetBrains
Teams automating code tasks in CI/CD
Developers who want to choose their own model, including local ones
Builders creating custom agents with the SDK
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for an open-source, model-agnostic coding agent with human-in-the-loop approval and a Plan/Act workflow. You pay for whichever model provider you connect.
requirements: VS Code, a JetBrains IDE, Node.js for the CLI, or macOS/Windows for the desktop app
An API key for a model provider, or a local model through Ollama or LM Studio

overview: Cline reads your project structure and makes coordinated changes, watching linter and compiler errors as it works. It runs terminal commands and watches their output. In Plan mode it explores and proposes a strategy; in Act mode it carries it out, with each file edit and command shown for approval.

Project rules in .clinerules files guide how it works in your codebase. It can be extended with plugins through the SDK or with MCP servers, can coordinate multi-agent teams, run scheduled agents on cron schedules, and connect to Slack, Telegram, Discord and other chat platforms.

The headless CLI fits scripts and CI: pipe in input, get JSON output. The @cline/sdk package exposes the same agent engine for building your own agents. Cline is Apache-2.0 licensed; the JetBrains plugin isn't open source.
